S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.

subtypes.Talkativeness: Speaking far more than usual and continuing to talk without rest.
subtypes.Rapid Speech: Speech speed is so fast that it is difficult for others to understand or interrupt.
subtypes.Pressured Speech: Cannot stop talking or tolerate silence due to an internal pressure to keep speaking.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.

subtypes.Responsiveness to Extraneous Stimuli: Attention is immediately drawn to trivial and unimportant stimuli nearby (e.g., noise, movement).
subtypes.Frequent Task Switching: Unable to finish one task and constantly shifting attention to new things, starting multiple tasks simultaneously.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Unable to focus on any activity for long, with attention constantly being scattered.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.

subtypes.Occupational Hyperactivity: Driving significantly more projects or work than usual in the workplace or academic setting.
subtypes.Social Hyperactivity: Becoming much more sociable and extroverted than usual, actively meeting and contacting people.
subtypes.Hypersexuality: Significantly increased interest in or activity regarding sex.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless non-goal-directed activity, such as pacing or hand-wringing, driven by an inability to sit still.

S041.name: Painful_Consequence_Behavior
S041.description: Excessive involvement in activities that have a high potential for painful consequences.

subtypes.Unrestrained Buying Sprees: Spending excessive amounts of money or shopping recklessly to a degree that creates financial distress for self and family.
subtypes.Foolish Business Investments: Making rash business investments or ventures without sufficient review.
subtypes.Sexual Indiscretions: Engaging in indiscriminate or risky sexual behavior that is out of character.
subtypes.Impulsive Risky Behavior: Excessively dangerous or foolish behavior, such as reckless driving or drug use, without considering the consequences.

symptom.disease_info: Bipolar I Disorder is characterized by at least one lifetime manic episode, typically lasting at least a week (or requiring hospitalization), often accompanied by marked functional impairment in work, relationships, or self-care. Manic episodes involve a distinct change from baseline mood and behavior, with elevated or irritable mood and increased energy, frequently leading to risky decisions or conflict, and they may alternate over time with episodes of depression or mixed features. Onset is often in late adolescence or early adulthood, but new or clearly impairing episodes can occur later in life, sometimes triggered or unmasked by stressors, sleep disruption, or medical changes. It is distinguished from Bipolar II Disorder by the presence of full mania (rather than hypomania), and from primary psychotic or substance-induced conditions by its episodic mood pattern and persistence beyond the direct effects of substances or medical illness.

patient.stressor: Hector had cut back to part‑time mentoring at the plant and was preparing for full retirement when his supervisor suggested a firm end date, which he experienced as a sudden loss of purpose despite his active community life. Around the same time, several younger relatives moved away for work, leaving him feeling compelled to "make up for it" by organizing more church events, youth mentoring sessions, and large family gatherings. Over the next month, his usual warm, steady presence shifted into nonstop planning of new community projects and impulsive commitments that he struggled to follow through on, creating tension with his wife and church leadership when he began showing up unannounced to push new ideas. After he drove several hours alone to visit a former coworker without telling anyone—alarming his family, given his age and health—they insisted he see his primary care physician, who, concerned about a late‑life mood episode rather than simple adjustment to retirement, referred him urgently to psychiatry.
patient.chief_complaint: “Lately I keep jumping into big plans and trips without thinking, and it’s starting to cause problems for my family.”

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: These past few weeks I swing between feeling on top of the world, like I’m the only one who really knows what needs to be done around here, to snapping at my wife or the pastor over the smallest pushback, and I can’t seem to dial it back even when I see I’m upsetting people.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: I wake up after just a few hours of sleep buzzing with energy, pacing around the house, rearranging my workshop, and making lists of projects for the church and the family until my wife begs me to just sit down and rest, which I feel physically unable to do.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.
S037.manifestation: Once I get going, I just keep talking—about retirement, new youth programs, trips we should take, old stories from the plant—jumping from one thing to the next so fast that people can’t get a word in, and I feel this pressure in my chest that won’t let me stop.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.
S039.manifestation: When I try to sit and plan something simple, like a church cookout, my mind keeps grabbing at every little thing—the bird outside, a text on my phone, a headline on TV—so I jump up to deal with each one and never actually finish what I started.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.
S040.manifestation: I’ve been signing up to lead extra Bible studies, organizing new mentoring groups, volunteering for every church repair, and calling relatives to plan big reunions, all at once, to the point that my calendar is crammed and I’m double‑booking myself almost every day.

S041.name: Painful_Consequence_Behavior
S041.description: Excessive involvement in activities that have a high potential for painful consequences.
S041.manifestation: I’ve been taking off on long drives without telling anyone, volunteering the little savings we have to help fund events I just dreamed up, and promising people I’ll host big gatherings or fix their houses even though my back and my bank account can’t really handle it, and only afterward do I realize how risky and unfair that is to my wife.
